sanskrit: asir viśasanaḥ khaḍgas tīkṣṇavartmā durāsadaḥ śrīgarbho vijayaś caiva dharmapālas tathaiva ca
english: Sword, Slayer, Blade, Keen-edged, Hard-to-withstand, Womb-of-Fortune, Victory, and likewise Guardian-of-Dharma —

sanskrit: agryaḥ praharaṇānāṃ ca khaḍgo mādravatīsuta maheśvarapraṇītaś ca purāṇe niścayaṃ gataḥ
english: the sword, O son of Mādravatī, is foremost among weapons, fashioned by Maheśvara, and so established by decree in the ancient lore.

sanskrit: pṛthus tūtpādayām āsa dhanur ādyam ariṃdama teneyaṃ pṛthivī pūrvaṃ vainyena parirakṣitā
english: It was Pṛthu who brought forth the first bow, O subduer of foes; and by him, the son of Vena, this earth was protected of old.

sanskrit: tad etad ārṣaṃ mādreya pramāṇaṃ kartum arhasi aseś ca pūjā kartavyā sadā yuddhaviśāradaiḥ
english: This teaching of the seers, O son of Mādrī, you should hold as authoritative; and the sword must ever be honored by those skilled in war.

sanskrit: ity eṣa prathamaḥ kalpo vyākhyātas te suvistaraḥ aser utpattisaṃsargo yathāvad bharatarṣabha
english: Thus this first rite has been expounded to you at full length, O bull of the Bhāratas — the origin and tradition of the sword, just as it is.

sanskrit: sarvathaitad iha śrutvā khaḍgasādhanam uttamam labhate puruṣaḥ kīrtiṃ pretya cānantyam aśnute
english: Hearing in every way this supreme discipline of the sword, a man attains fame in this world and, after death, partakes of the eternal.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktavati bhīṣme tu tūṣṇīṃbhūte yudhiṣṭhiraḥ papracchāvasaraṃ gatvā bhrātṝn vidurapañcamān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Bhīṣma had spoken thus and fallen silent, Yudhiṣṭhira, finding the moment, drew aside and questioned his brothers, with Vidura the fifth among them.

sanskrit: dharme cārthe ca kāme ca lokavṛttiḥ samāhitā teṣāṃ garīyān katamo madhyamaḥ ko laghuś ca kaḥ
english: "The conduct of the world rests upon dharma, artha, and kāma. Of these, which is the weightiest, which the middling, and which the least?

sanskrit: kasmiṃś cātmā niyantavyas trivargavijayāya vai saṃtuṣṭā naiṣṭhikaṃ vākyaṃ yathāvad vaktum arhatha
english: And in which of them should the self be governed, so as to master the threefold aim? Of one accord, you ought to speak the decisive word, just as it is."

sanskrit: tato 'rthagatitattvajñaḥ prathamaṃ pratibhānavān jagāda viduro vākyaṃ dharmaśāstram anusmaran
english: Then Vidura, who knew the true workings of worldly gain and was ready of wit, spoke first, calling to mind the treatises of dharma.

sanskrit: bāhuśrutyaṃ tapas tyāgaḥ śraddhā yajñakriyā kṣamā bhāvaśuddhir dayā satyaṃ saṃyamaś cātmasaṃpadaḥ
english: "Wide learning, austerity, renunciation, faith, the performance of sacrifice, forbearance, purity of intent, compassion, truth, and self-restraint — these are the riches of the soul.

sanskrit: etad evābhipadyasva mā te bhūc calitaṃ manaḥ etan mūlau hi dharmārthāv etad ekapadaṃ hitam
english: To this alone hold fast; let not your mind waver. On this dharma and artha are rooted; this is the one sure path to good.

sanskrit: dharmeṇaivarṣayas tīrṇā dharme lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ dharmeṇa devā divigā dharme cārthaḥ samāhitaḥ
english: By dharma the seers crossed beyond; on dharma the worlds are established; by dharma the gods reached heaven; and in dharma is artha contained.

sanskrit: dharmo rājan guṇaśreṣṭho madhyamo hy artha ucyate kāmo yavīyān iti ca pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ tasmād dharmapradhānena bhavitavyaṃ yatātmanā
english: Dharma, O king, is highest in worth; artha is called the middling; and kāma the least — so the wise declare. Therefore one should be self-controlled, holding dharma foremost."

sanskrit: samāptavacane tasminn arthaśāstraviśāradaḥ pārtho vākyārthatattvajño jagau vākyam atandritaḥ
english: When his speech was done, Pārtha — versed in the science of statecraft and knowing the true meaning of words — spoke without weariness:

sanskrit: karmabhūmir iyaṃ rājann iha vārttā praśasyate kṛṣivāṇijyagorakṣyaṃ śilpāni vividhāni ca
english: "This is the field of action, O king, and here livelihood is praised — farming, trade, the herding of cattle, and the various crafts.

sanskrit: artha ity eva sarveṣāṃ karmaṇām avyatikramaḥ na ṛte 'rthena vartete dharmakāmāv iti śrutiḥ
english: It is wealth that underlies all undertakings without exception. Without wealth neither dharma nor kāma can be pursued — so says the sacred word.

sanskrit: vijayī hy arthavān dharmam ārādhayitum uttamam kāmaṃ ca carituṃ śakto duṣprāpam akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: For the man of wealth, victorious, is able to honor the highest dharma and to pursue desire — both beyond the reach of those who have not mastered themselves.

sanskrit: arthasyāvayavāv etau dharmakāmāv iti śrutiḥ arthasiddhyā hi nirvṛttāv ubhāv etau bhaviṣyataḥ
english: Dharma and kāma are but the limbs of artha — so says the sacred word; for once wealth is secured, these two are brought to their fulfillment.

sanskrit: udbhūtārthaṃ hi puruṣaṃ viśiṣṭatarayonayaḥ brahmāṇam iva bhūtāni satataṃ paryupāsate
english: For the man whose fortune has risen, even those of nobler birth attend upon him without ceasing, as living creatures attend upon Brahmā.

sanskrit: jaṭājinadharā dāntāḥ paṅkadigdhā jitendriyāḥ muṇḍā nistantavaś cāpi vasanty arthārthinaḥ pṛthak
english: Bearing matted locks and deerskins, self-disciplined, smeared with mud, their senses conquered, shaven, casting off the sacred thread — even such men dwell apart, each a seeker of gain.

sanskrit: kāṣāyavasanāś cānye śmaśrulā hrīsusaṃvṛtāḥ vidvāṃsaś caiva śāntāś ca muktāḥ sarvaparigrahaiḥ
english: Others, robed in ochre, bearded, well-cloaked in modesty, learned and serene, freed of all possessions —

sanskrit: arthārthinaḥ santi ke cid apare svargakāṅkṣiṇaḥ kulapratyāgamāś caike svaṃ svaṃ mārgam anuṣṭhitāḥ
english: some among them seek gain, others long for heaven, and some uphold the customs of their line — each following his own road.

sanskrit: āstikā nāstikāś caiva niyatāḥ saṃyame pare aprajñānaṃ tamobhūtaṃ prajñānaṃ tu prakāśatā
english: Believers and unbelievers alike, bound and intent upon self-restraint — ignorance is a thing of darkness, but knowledge is light.

sanskrit: bhṛtyān bhogair dviṣo daṇḍair yo yojayati so 'rthavān etan matimatāṃ śreṣṭha mataṃ mama yathātatham anayos tu nibodha tvaṃ vacanaṃ vākyakaṇṭhayoḥ
english: He who plies his servants with enjoyments and his foes with chastisement — he is the man of substance. This, O best of the wise, is my view, just as it stands. But now mark the words of these two whose speech is poised upon the throat."

sanskrit: tato dharmārthakuśalau mādrīputrāv anantaram nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca vākyaṃ jagadatuḥ param
english: Then, next in turn, the sons of Mādrī — Nakula and Sahadeva, skilled in dharma and artha — spoke their excellent word:

sanskrit: āsīnaś ca śayānaś ca vicarann api ca sthitaḥ arthayogaṃ dṛḍhaṃ kuryād yogair uccāvacair api
english: "Sitting, lying, moving about, or standing still, a man should pursue gain steadfastly, by means high and low alike.

sanskrit: asmiṃs tu vai susaṃvṛtte durlabhe paramapriye iha kāmān avāpnoti pratyakṣaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: For when this wealth — hard to win, most dear — is well secured, one attains all desires in this very world, plainly; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yo 'rtho dharmeṇa saṃyukto dharmo yaś cārthasaṃyutaḥ madhv ivāmṛtasaṃyuktaṃ tasmād etau matāv iha
english: Wealth joined to dharma, and dharma joined to wealth, are like honey blended with nectar; therefore both of these are esteemed in this world.

sanskrit: anarthasya na kāmo 'sti tathārtho 'dharmiṇaḥ kutaḥ tasmād udvijate loko dharmārthād yo bahiṣkṛtaḥ
english: For the man without wealth there is no kāma; and whence comes wealth to him who lacks dharma? Therefore the world shrinks from one who is cast out from dharma and artha.

sanskrit: tasmād dharmapradhānena sādhyo 'rthaḥ saṃyatātmanā viśvasteṣu ca bhūteṣu kalpate sarva eva hi
english: Therefore wealth should be sought by one who is self-controlled, holding dharma foremost; for among trusting creatures everything alike comes to fruition.

sanskrit: dharmaṃ samācaret pūrvaṃ tathārthaṃ dharmasaṃyutam tataḥ kāmaṃ caret paścāt siddhārthasya hi tat phalam
english: Let a man first practice dharma, then wealth conjoined with dharma, and only afterward pursue desire; for that is the fruit reserved for one whose purpose is accomplished."

sanskrit: virematus tu tad vākyam uktvā tāv aśvinoḥ sutau bhīmasenas tadā vākyam idaṃ vaktuṃ pracakrame
english: When the two sons of the Aśvins had spoken these words and fallen silent, Bhīmasena then set himself to say this:

sanskrit: nākāmaḥ kāmayaty arthaṃ nākāmo dharmam icchati nākāmaḥ kāmayāno 'sti tasmāt kāmo viśiṣyate
english: "Without desire none longs for wealth; without desire none wishes for dharma; without desire there is no one who craves at all — therefore kāma is supreme.

sanskrit: kāmena yuktā ṛṣayas tapasy eva samāhitāḥ palāśaphalamūlāśā vāyubhakṣāḥ susaṃyatāḥ
english: It is moved by desire that the seers are intent upon their austerities, feeding on leaves, fruits, and roots, living on air, well-restrained.

sanskrit: vedopavādeṣv apare yuktāḥ svādhyāyapāragāḥ śrāddhayajñakriyāyāṃ ca tathā dānapratigrahe
english: Others give themselves to the recitation of the Veda, masters of private study, and to the rites of śrāddha and sacrifice, and to giving and receiving gifts.

sanskrit: vaṇijaḥ karṣakā gopāḥ kāravaḥ śilpinas tathā daivakarmakṛtaś caiva yuktāḥ kāmena karmasu
english: Merchants, farmers, herdsmen, craftsmen, artisans, and those who perform rites for the gods — all are driven by desire in their labors.

sanskrit: samudraṃ cāviśanty anye narāḥ kāmena saṃyutāḥ kāmo hi vividhākāraḥ sarvaṃ kāmena saṃtatam
english: Still other men, urged by desire, plunge into the sea. For desire takes manifold forms; all things are strung through with desire.

sanskrit: nāsti nāsīn nābhaviṣyad bhūtaṃ kāmātmakāt param etat sāraṃ mahārāja dharmārthāv atra saṃśritau
english: There is not, was not, nor shall ever be a being greater than one whose essence is desire. This is the very pith of it, O great king; dharma and artha both rest within it.

sanskrit: navanītaṃ yathā dadhnas tathā kāmo 'rthadharmataḥ śreyas tailaṃ ca piṇyākād dhṛtaṃ śreya udaśvitaḥ
english: As butter is the best of curds, so is kāma the best of wealth and dharma. Oil is better than oil-cake, and clarified butter better than buttermilk.

sanskrit: śreyaḥ puṣpaphalaṃ kāṣṭhāt kāmo dharmārthayor varaḥ puṣpato madhv iva rasaḥ kāmāt saṃjāyate sukham
english: Flower and fruit are better than mere wood; so is kāma the choicest of dharma and artha. As nectar's sweetness is born from the flower, so from desire is happiness born.

sanskrit: sucāruveṣābhir alaṃkṛtābhir; madotkaṭābhiḥ priyavādinībhiḥ ramasva yoṣābhir upetya kāmaṃ; kāmo hi rājaṃs tarasābhipātī
english: With women fairly adorned, lavishly decked, flushed with passion and sweet of speech, draw near and take your pleasure at will; for desire, O king, swoops down with sudden force.

sanskrit: buddhir mamaiṣā pariṣat sthitasya; mā bhūd vicāras tava dharmaputra syāt saṃhitaṃ sadbhir aphalgusāraṃ; sametya vākyaṃ param ānṛśaṃsyam
english: Such is my thought, set forth here in this assembly. Let there be no hesitation in you, O son of Dharma. May the word agreed upon, framed by the good and of no hollow substance, prove in the end the highest of all — compassion."

sanskrit: dharmārthakāmāḥ samam eva sevyā; yas tv ekasevī sa naro jaghanyaḥ dvayos tu dakṣaṃ pravadanti madhyaṃ; sa uttamo yo niratas trivarge
english: "Dharma, artha, and kāma should be cultivated equally. The man who serves but one of them is the lowest; him who is adept in two they call the middling; but he is highest who is devoted to all three."

sanskrit: prājñaḥ suhṛc candanasāralipto; vicitramālyābharaṇair upetaḥ tato vacaḥ saṃgrahavigraheṇa; proktvā yavīyān virarāma bhīmaḥ
english: Wise and kindly, anointed with sandal essence, decked in fair garlands and ornaments, Bhīma the younger, having spoken his word both in sum and in detail, then fell silent.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād atha dharmarājo; vākyāni teṣām anucintya samyak uvāca vācāvitathaṃ smayan vai; bahuśruto dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ
english: Then after a moment the Dharma King, having pondered well their words, spoke with a smile, in speech that was free of falsehood — he, the widely learned, the foremost of the upholders of dharma:

sanskrit: niḥsaṃśayaṃ niścitadharmaśāstrāḥ; sarve bhavanto viditapramāṇāḥ vijñātukāmasya mameha vākyam; uktaṃ yad vai naiṣṭhikaṃ tac chrutaṃ me iha tv avaśyaṃ gadato mamāpi; vākyaṃ nibodhadhvam ananyabhāvāḥ
english: "Beyond doubt, you are all sure in the science of dharma and well versed in its standards. The decisive word you have spoken to me, who wished to understand — that I have heard. Yet now hear without distraction the word that I, in turn, must needs declare.

sanskrit: yo vai na pāpe nirato na puṇye; nārthe na dharme manujo na kāme vimuktadoṣaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcanaḥ; sa mucyate duḥkhasukhārthasiddheḥ
english: The man who clings neither to sin nor to merit, neither to wealth nor to dharma nor to desire, freed of all faults, to whom a clod and gold are alike — he is released from the whole pursuit of pleasure and pain.

sanskrit: bhūtāni jātīmaraṇānvitāni; jarāvikāraiś ca samanvitāni bhūyaś ca tais taiḥ pratibodhitāni; mokṣaṃ praśaṃsanti na taṃ ca vidmaḥ
english: All beings are bound up with birth and death, beset by age and decay, and roused again and again by these afflictions; they extol release — yet that release we do not know.

sanskrit: snehe nabaddhasya na santi tānīty; evaṃ svayaṃbhūr bhagavān uvāca budhāś ca nirvāṇaparā vadanti; tasmān na kuryāt priyam apriyaṃ ca
english: "For him who is not bound by attachment, these afflictions exist not" — so the Self-Existent Lord declared. And the wise, intent upon nirvāṇa, say the same; therefore one should make for oneself neither the dear nor the hateful.

sanskrit: etat pradhānaṃ na tu kāmakāro; yathā niyukto 'smi tathā carāmi bhūtāni sarvāṇi vidhir niyuṅkte; vidhir balīyān iti vitta sarve
english: This is the principal thing — not the willful following of desire. As I am ordained, so do I act. Ordinance appoints all beings to their tasks; know all of you that ordinance is the stronger.

sanskrit: na karmaṇāpnoty anavāpyam arthaṃ; yad bhāvi sarvaṃ bhavatīti vitta trivargahīno 'pi hi vindate 'rthaṃ; tasmād idaṃ lokahitāya guhyam
english: By action one cannot win what is not to be won; whatever is to be, all of it comes to pass — know this. Even one bereft of the threefold aim may yet find his gain; therefore this mystery is set forth for the welfare of the world.

sanskrit: tatas tad agryaṃ vacanaṃ manonugaṃ; samastam ājñāya tato 'tihetumat tadā praṇeduś ca jaharṣire ca te; kurupravīrāya ca cakrur añjalīn
english: Then, when they had heard that foremost word, pleasing to the mind and abounding in reason, those gathered there raised their voices and rejoiced, and folded their hands in homage to the hero of the Kurus.

sanskrit: sucāruvarṇākṣaraśabdabhūṣitāṃ; manonugāṃ nirdhutavākyakaṇṭakām niśamya tāṃ pārthiva pārthabhāṣitāṃ; giraṃ narendrāḥ praśaśaṃsur eva te punaś ca papraccha saridvarāsutaṃ; tataḥ paraṃ dharmam ahīnasattvaḥ
english: Having heard that speech of Pārtha — adorned with fair letters, syllables, and sounds, pleasing to the mind, cleansed of every thorn of language — the lords of men praised it, O king. Then once more, undiminished in spirit, he questioned the son of the great river concerning the further dharma.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pitāmaha mahāprājña kurūṇāṃ kīrtivardhana praśnaṃ kaṃ cit pravakṣyāmi tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O grandsire, deeply wise, increaser of the glory of the Kurus, I shall put a certain question; this you ought to expound to me.

sanskrit: kīdṛśā mānavāḥ saumyāḥ kaiḥ prītiḥ paramā bhavet āyatyāṃ ca tadātve ca ke kṣamās tān vadasva me
english: What manner of men are agreeable? With whom does the highest affection arise? Who are fit to be trusted, both for the long term and the present moment? Of these, tell me.

sanskrit: na hi tatra dhanaṃ sphītaṃ na ca saṃbandhibāndhavāḥ tiṣṭhanti yatra suhṛdas tiṣṭhantīti matir mama
english: For neither abundant wealth nor kinsmen and relations avail there where true friends stand fast — such is my conviction.

sanskrit: durlabho hi suhṛc chrotā durlabhaś ca hitaḥ suhṛt etad dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha sarvaṃ vyākhyātum arhasi
english: Hard to find is a friend who will listen, and hard to find a friend who seeks one's good. All this, O best of the upholders of dharma, you ought to explain.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca saṃdheyān puruṣān rājann asaṃdheyāṃś ca tattvataḥ vadato me nibodha tvaṃ nikhilena yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: The men with whom alliance may be made, O king, and those with whom it may not — hear of them truly, in full, from me as I speak, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: lubdhaḥ krūras tyaktadharmā nikṛtaḥ śaṭha eva ca kṣudraḥ pāpasamācāraḥ sarvaśaṅkī tathālasaḥ
english: The greedy, the cruel, the man who has abandoned dharma, the deceitful and the crooked, the base, the man of evil conduct, the suspicious of all, and the sluggish;

sanskrit: dīrghasūtro 'nṛjuḥ kaṣṭo gurudārapradharṣakaḥ vyasane yaḥ parityāgī durātmā nirapatrapaḥ
english: the procrastinator, the dishonest, the harsh, the violator of an elder's wife, he who forsakes a friend in distress, the wicked-souled and shameless;

sanskrit: sarvataḥ pāpadarśī ca nāstiko vedanindakaḥ saṃprakīrṇendriyo loke yaḥ kāmanirataś caret
english: he who sees evil on every side, the unbeliever and reviler of the Veda, and the man who roves the world with senses scattered, given over to lust;

sanskrit: asatyo lokavidviṣṭaḥ samaye cānavasthitaḥ piśuno 'thākṛtaprajño matsarī pāpaniścayaḥ
english: the false, the hated of the world, the man who keeps no covenant, the slanderer, the untrained in wisdom, the envious, the fixed in evil purpose;

sanskrit: duḥśīlo 'thākṛtātmā ca nṛśaṃsaḥ kitavas tathā mitrair arthakṛtī nityam icchaty arthaparaś ca yaḥ
english: the ill-natured, the undisciplined in self, the savage, the gambler, and he who ever exploits his friends for gain, intent on profit alone;

sanskrit: vahataś ca yathāśakti yo na tuṣyati mandadhīḥ amitram iva yo bhuṅkte sadā mitraṃ nararṣabha
english: the dull-witted man who is never content though one serves him to the utmost of one's power, and who feeds upon a friend as though upon a foe, O bull among men;

sanskrit: asthānakrodhano yaś ca akasmāc ca virajyate suhṛdaś caiva kalyāṇān āśu tyajati kilbiṣī
english: he who is angered without cause and grows estranged for no reason, and the sinner who swiftly casts off well-meaning friends;

sanskrit: alpe 'py apakṛte mūḍhas tathājñānāt kṛte 'pi ca kāryopasevī mitreṣu mitradveṣī narādhipa
english: the fool who takes offense at the slightest wrong, even at one done in ignorance, who courts his friends only when he has need of them yet hates them at heart, O lord of men;

sanskrit: śatrur mitramukho yaś ca jihmaprekṣī vilobhanaḥ na rajyati ca kalyāṇe yas tyajet tādṛśaṃ naram
english: and the enemy who wears a friend's face, the man of crooked glance, the seducer who takes no delight in what is good — such a man one should forsake.

sanskrit: pānapo dveṣaṇaḥ krūro nirghṛṇaḥ paruṣas tathā paropatāpī mitradhruk tathā prāṇivadhe rataḥ
english: The drunkard, the hateful, the cruel, the pitiless and harsh, the tormentor of others, the betrayer of friends, and he who delights in the slaying of living things;

sanskrit: kṛtaghnaś cādhamo loke na saṃdheyaḥ kathaṃ cana chidrānveṣī na saṃdheyaḥ saṃdheyān api me śṛṇu
english: the ingrate, basest in the world — with such a one alliance may in no way be made; nor with the man who hunts for another's weaknesses. Now hear from me those with whom alliance may be made.

sanskrit: kulīnā vākyasaṃpannā jñānavijñānakovidāḥ mitrajñāś ca kṛtajñāś ca sarvajñāḥ śokavarjitāḥ
english: Men of good birth, gifted in speech, skilled in knowledge and discernment, faithful to friends and grateful, all-knowing and free of grief;

sanskrit: mādhuryaguṇasaṃpannāḥ satyasaṃdhā jitendriyāḥ vyāyāmaśīlāḥ satataṃ bhṛtaputrāḥ kulodgatāḥ
english: endowed with the grace of sweetness, true to their pledges, masters of their senses, ever diligent in effort, who maintain their sons and dependents, sprung from noble line;

sanskrit: rūpavanto guṇopetās tathālubdhā jitaśramāḥ doṣair viyuktāḥ prathitais te grāhyāḥ pārthivena ha
english: comely, possessed of virtues, free from greed, conquerors of fatigue, untouched by the well-known faults — these, indeed, a king should embrace.

sanskrit: yathāśaktisamācārāḥ santas tuṣyanti hi prabho nāsthāne krodhavantaś ca na cākasmād virāgiṇaḥ
english: For the good, O lord, are content with service rendered to the best of one's power; they are not wrathful out of season, nor estranged without cause.

sanskrit: viraktāś ca na ruṣyanti manasāpy arthakovidāḥ ātmānaṃ pīḍayitvāpi suhṛtkāryaparāyaṇāḥ na virajyanti mitrebhyo vāso raktam ivāvikam
english: Even when estranged they harbor no anger, not even in mind, those skilled in worldly affairs; bent on a friend's cause even at cost to themselves, they no more lose their bond with friends than dye loses its hold upon wool.

sanskrit: doṣāṃś ca lobhamohādīn artheṣu yuvatiṣv atha na darśayanti suhṛdāṃ viśvastā bandhuvatsalāḥ
english: Trusted and tender toward kin, they show no faults of greed and delusion and the like toward their friends, whether in matters of wealth or of women.

sanskrit: loṣṭakāñcanatulyārthāḥ suhṛtsv aśaṭhabuddhayaḥ ye caranty anabhīmānā nisṛṣṭārthavibhūṣaṇāḥ saṃgṛhṇantaḥ parijanaṃ svāmyarthaparamāḥ sadā
english: To whom a clod and gold are of equal worth, guileless of mind toward friends, who walk without conceit, freely lavishing wealth and adornments, sustaining their retinue, ever devoted to their master's good —

sanskrit: īdṛśaiḥ puruṣaśreṣṭhaiḥ saṃdhiṃ yaḥ kurute nṛpaḥ tasya vistīryate rāṣṭraṃ jyotsnā grahapater iva
english: the king who makes alliance with such excellent men sees his realm spread wide, as the moonlight of the lord of planets spreads abroad.

sanskrit: śāstranityā jitakrodhā balavanto raṇapriyāḥ kṣāntāḥ śīlaguṇopetāḥ saṃdheyāḥ puruṣottamāḥ
english: Steadfast in the scriptures, masters of their anger, mighty, loving battle, patient, endowed with character and virtue — such are the best of men, fit for alliance.

sanskrit: ye ca doṣasamāyuktā narāḥ proktā mayānagha teṣām apy adhamo rājan kṛtaghno mitraghātakaḥ tyaktavyaḥ sa durācāraḥ sarveṣām iti niścayaḥ
english: And of those men endowed with faults whom I have named, O sinless one, the basest, O king, is the ingrate, the slayer of friends; that man of evil conduct must be forsaken by all — such is the settled conclusion.
